The '''1920 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 34th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 9 May 1920 but wasn't completed until 14 May 1922 due to the ongoing [[Irish War of Independence|War of Independence]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keane |first=Eoin |date=2020-04-20 |title=Hurling history: The struggle to play Cork and Limerick at the height of the War of Independence |url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40121258.html |access-date=5 March 2025|publisher=Echo Live |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-20461696.html|title=What type of men win an All-Ireland in time of war?|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 October 2017|accessdate=20 August 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

[[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1919 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|defending champions]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/centuryireland/articles/cork-defeat-dublin-in-all-ireland-hurling-decider|title=Cork defeat Dublin in All-Ireland hurling decider|publisher=Century Ireland|date=|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/not-since-1903-1919-have-cork-gone-so-long-without-a-hurling-all-ireland-has-their-time-come-again/a/135905739.html|title=Not since 1903-1919 have Cork gone so long without a hurling All-Ireland, has their time come again?|publisher=Irish Independent|date=28 July 2018|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref>

The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 14 May 1922 between [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] and Cork, in what was their [[Cork–Dublin hurling rivalry#All-time results|fifth championship meeting overall]] and a second consecutive meeting in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dublingaa.ie/news/recent-meetings-dublin-v-cork-hurling|title=Recent meetings: Dublin v Cork (hurling)|publisher=Dublin GAA website|date=29 July 2021|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref> Dublin won the match by 4–09 to 4–03 to claim their third All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1917 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|three years]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/centuryireland/articles/dublin-victorious-in-deferred-all-ireland-hurling-final|title=Dublin victorious in deferred All-Ireland hurling final|publisher=Century Ireland|date=|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/100th-anniversary-of-limerick-duo-winning-all-ireland-hurling-title-with-dublin-8024509|title=100th anniversary of Limerick duo winning All-Ireland hurling title with Dublin|publisher=Limerick Live|date=12 December 2020|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref>

==Teams==

A total of fourteen teams contested the championship, the same as the [[1919 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|previous championship]]; however, there were some changes of personnel, with [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] replacing [[Laois GAA|Laois]] in the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]].

==Championship statistics==
===Miscellaneous===

* The Munster final between Cork and Limerick was originally scheduled for 29 August 1920; however, due to the [[hunger strike]] of the [[Lord Mayor of Cork]] [[Terence MacSwiney]], the game did not take place until 2 April 1922.
* Not one of the Dublin hurling team that won the All-Ireland final was born in [[County Dublin|Dublin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-08-05 |title=Limerick GAA notes – latest news from 19 different clubs |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/877194/limerick-gaa-notes-latest-news-from-19-different-clubs.html |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=www.limerickleader.ie |language=en}}</ref>
